short: Wi-Fi backscatter lip sensing (M05) and subword sentence output (M08) are standard; open-sentence decoding is untested, with no sentence-disjoint split and 36.87% WER.
position: The paper [@tian2026lipsiri] changes the sensor (M05), a passive Wi-Fi backscatter tag near the face, and the output (M08), subword sentences instead of class labels. Both are standard: contactless radio-frequency sensing is already usual, Wi-Fi lip reading predates it [@hameed2022rf], and face-worn RFID tags already sense speech by backscatter (Table I). The open-sentence claim is untested: 340 scripted sentences, each read at least twice, are split 80/20 at random, so test sentences very likely also appear in training (inference), and no unseen-sentence test exists. The headline 36.87% WER is worse than the visual baseline's 32.3% in the same room (§VI-B), although the text calls the two comparable. The held-out-user test (M12, standard) is the paper's strongest evidence.
